questions.question: Explain the difference between an interest rate and interest, using Thabo's savings account as the example, and state the unit each one carries.
questions.expected_answer: The interest rate is a percentage per time period — 8% per year — a speed, not money. The interest is the rand amount produced when the rate acts on the principal: 8% of R3 000 is R240. Rates carry percent per period; interest carries rand.

questions.question: Show, year by year, how R3 000 at 8% per year grows over two years when the interest stays in the account, and explain why year two's interest is larger.
questions.expected_answer: Year one: 8% of R3 000 is R240, balance R3 240. Year two: 8% of R3 240 is R259,20, balance R3 499,20. Year two is larger because the first year's interest remained in the account and itself earned interest — the balance, not the original deposit, is what the rate acts on.

questions.question: Why can the mashonisa's 30% not be compared directly with the bank's 20%, and what is the honest comparison?
questions.expected_answer: The periods differ: 20% is per year, 30% is per month. On R3 000 the bank charges R600 per year while the mashonisa charges R900 every month. Converted to the same period, 30% per month is 360% per year — eighteen times the bank's 20%. Rates must wear the same time period before being compared.
